requirements.title: AI mathematics override
requirements.summary: AI uses COMP_SCI 212-0 instead of the generic MATH 228-2 core requirement. ES_APPM 252-1/252-2 can substitute for the corresponding MATH 228-1/228-2 sequence; this does not erase the AI discrete-mathematics requirement.

requirements.title: Science lab and duplicate restrictions
requirements.summary: Science labs count only together with their corresponding lectures. EARTH 210/203, EARTH 214/201 and EARTH 215/202 carry explicit duplicate-credit restrictions. The separate duplicate-course rules also apply.

requirements.title: Seven-unit humanities/social science theme
requirements.summary: Seven courses, with at most five in either category, at least three thematically related, and ordinarily no more than three at 100 level. AP/IB/transfer credit may qualify. The catalog says submit by winter of junior year; public theme guidance instead says end of sophomore year. Full public subject rules are mapped separately.

requirements.title: Five unrestricted electives
requirements.summary: Any credit-bearing university course may fill the five unrestricted electives, subject to duplicate-credit and other degree policies.

requirements.title: BSE relationship and unique major credit
requirements.summary: The BSE AI major may be pursued in McCormick or as a second major from another undergraduate school. At least 11 of its 22 major units must be unique, unused in other majors, minors or certificates. Adding AI to a discipline-specific McCormick BS is a second major, not the multiple-BS arrangement. This record maps the McCormick degree; another home school retains its own degree rules.

requirements.title: Transfer-credit cap and approval
requirements.summary: At most four externally completed units may count in the 22-unit major, with both department and school approval. Other degree categories are not subject to this four-unit cap; the University Registration Requirement still applies.

requirements.title: Degree and major grades
requirements.summary: At least 2.0 GPA in all degree units and separately in the 22-unit major. At most three major units may have D grades. External courses used for McCormick requirements need C or better.

requirements.title: Degree application and curriculum changes
requirements.summary: Apply for the degree through MAS a year before graduation. Students encountering changes while enrolled may choose an entire curriculum used during their enrollment; extended interruptions normally trigger new requirements.

requirements.title: Catalog P/N limits
requirements.summary: No more than eight P/N units toward the 48-unit degree, and at most one per quarter in years one/two. No P/N in mathematics, engineering foundations, sciences or design/communication/innovation. Theme permits any 300-level course but at most four at 100/200 level. Major P/N eligibility is delegated to the department; do not assume permission.

requirements.title: Approved placement and exemptions
requirements.summary: Approved tests or individually reviewed prior coursework may grant credit or an exemption reducing required units. Such approval never removes the separate registration requirement; no particular waiver is presumed.

requirements.title: Registration and Northwestern-credit minimums
requirements.summary: First-year single-degree entrants need nine registered quarters and 32 earned Northwestern units; transfers need six quarters and 21 units. These are separate from the 48-unit degree total.

requirements.title: Approved dual-school registration minimums
requirements.summary: For approved dual bachelor’s degrees across schools, first-year entrants need eleven quarters/42 Northwestern units; transfers need nine quarters/32 units. Adding a second major does not itself create a dual degree.

requirements.title: Qualifying quarters versus earned credits
requirements.summary: A registered quarter needs at least two full units of Northwestern coursework under Northwestern faculty. Passing and listed nonpassing/W grades can count toward quarter registration; NR cannot. Only earned A–D or P credit counts toward the unit minimum. Co-op and ordinary transferred study-abroad credit do not qualify; at least two units of Northwestern-faculty -SA study-abroad courses do.

requirements.title: Rare registration-waiver petition
requirements.summary: Consult school advising; petition only within two quarters of graduation. Exceptions normally address credit amounts; reducing required quarters is considered only for University error. Eligibility is not an approved waiver.

requirements.title: Social & Behavioral Sciences eligible departments

requirements.title: Theme structure and approval
requirements.summary: Use seven courses, at most five in one category, with at least three related and a title/narrative. Three 100-level courses maximum, or four if three are foreign language. Fractional-unit courses combine; petition Weinberg first-year seminars. AP/IB may qualify. No course may also fill another of the 48 McCormick requirements. Public deadline is end of sophomore year, differing from the catalog’s junior-winter deadline.

requirements.title: Theme approvals and restrictions
requirements.summary: Theme cannot be waived, including for co-op or a second major. Study-abroad theme credit needs MAS petition with an English syllabus. Denied plans may go to the Curriculum Committee, whose decision is final. Planned courses may receive conditional approval and revisions. Research methods/statistics/accounting/econometrics and Engineering coursework are excluded; non-engineering second-major courses can count if otherwise eligible.

requirements.title: Public registration approval rules
requirements.summary: Each quarter requires an adviser meeting and approved MAS study plan before the hold is released. Regular registration caps at 4.99 units; up to 5.5 may be added in drop/add, and higher loads need associate-dean permission. Conflicting times need both instructors’ signed permission. McCormick does not ordinarily participate in preregistration. Study-abroad return-quarter plans need approval before departure sign-off.

requirements.title: Public transfer review and source discrepancy
requirements.summary: Transfer without a direct Northwestern equivalent requires curriculum petition for any category except unrestricted electives. Review proposed US coursework before beginning it. Departmental approval is needed for at most four major transfer units and departments may impose tighter limits. This page calls the major 21 units; the current AI/catalog major is 22. The discrepancy is retained; no 21-unit AI requirement is inferred.

requirements.title: Operational P/N approvals
requirements.summary: Only courses offering Student Option can use P/N; McCormick cannot override another school and says its own courses do not offer that option. Confirm permitted requirement use before changing grading. Deadline is Friday of week eight. Years one/two: one course per quarter; later additional courses need the P/N form. Public page says eight P courses, catalog says eight units; no equivalence is assumed. AI-specific major P/N permission remains unverified.

requirements.title: Duplicate courses are not substitutions
requirements.summary: Only one of duplicate courses may satisfy a McCormick degree/certificate requirement; taking a duplicate does not replace a specifically required course and cannot supply an unrestricted elective. CS110/111 duplication is conditional on taking111 first; CS230/211 on taking211 first. Other published duplicate pairs and bundles still require mapping; do not treat this bounded observation as the full list.

requirements.title: Post-matriculation transfer approval
requirements.summary: Consult school/major advisers and submit a proposal with course description or syllabus before outside coursework; a month of lead time is recommended. Review proceeds through home school, relevant department and applicable credential adviser, then student and final school approval. Final official transcript is required; advance approval does not guarantee final articulation. McCormick may accept two-year/community-college credit with approval.

requirements.title: Mathematics transfer format restriction
requirements.summary: Mathematics post-matriculation transfer courses must be in person at a fully accredited four-year institution; online coursework is not accepted by the department.

requirements.title: Study-abroad credit approval
requirements.summary: Follow the approved study-abroad process before foreign coursework, including the published home-country exceptions. After program evaluation and official transcript review, eligible credit is initially general elective credit; school petition is needed to designate a Northwestern course or apply it to major/minor requirements. Program-specific conversion ratios apply; no universal conversion is inferred.
